Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-25

Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Redwood - Sofia Martinez (AE), Daniel Cho (SE), Priya Kapoor (CSM); AzureHealth - Michael Chen (CISO), Dr. Laura Price (Privacy Officer), James Park (Lead ML Engineer)
---
Auto Summary (brief): security & privacy deep-dive. Discussed SOC 2/ISO attestations, RBAC/SSO/SCIM, audit logs retention, encryption and customer-managed KMS, data residency (US), prompt/content retention and deletion, PHI/PII handling and BAA options, confirmation that Redwood does not train models on customer data in hosted deployments; private/on-prem options covered. Agreed next steps: share artifacts, send DPA/BAA, schedule PoC kickoff.
---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. We'll do a quick intros then jump into security stuff — Daniel will lead the technical bits.
[00:18] Michael: Thanks Sofia. Quick note, we're a health org so PHI is a hard constraint for us. We want to understand retention, BAAs, and how prompts might be stored.
[00:30] Sofia: Absolutely, that's top of the agenda. Daniel, can you take us through the architecture and the data handling points?
[00:38] Daniel: Yeah hi all. So at a high level Redwood provides hosted, dedicated and private deployments. For data handling specifics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are in place — we can share the reports under NDA — and we support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning, RBAC for account-level roles, and detailed audit logs that are exportable.
[01:05] Laura: When you say audit logs are exportable, what's the retention window? Can we push them to our SIEM?
[01:12] Daniel: Good question. By default audit logs retained 90 days in the hosted product, but you can push them via syslog/S3 export to your SIEM or a bucket for longer retention. Dedicated/Private gives you full control of retention since logs can live inside your VPC.
[01:30] James: And encryption? We need customer-managed keys for encryption at rest. HSM-backed KMS ideally.
[01:37] Daniel: We support CMEK in Dedicated and Private — you can bring your own KMS keys (HSM/KMS) and we integrate with common providers. In hosted we also encrypt at rest and in transit, but CMEK is typically for dedicated/private. (note: transcript sometimes shows K-M-S as spelled)
[01:58] Michael: Okay. Most important: prompt/content retention. If our engineers send PHI in prompts, is that stored? Is it used for training models?
[02:09] Sofia: Short answer: Redwood does not use customer prompt/content to train public models. We can provide written confirmation. We also have configurable retention policies — for hosted customers default is 30 days for full transcripts and prompts for troubleshooting, but we can set retention lower or disable retention for an account / use case, and Private deployments can be configured to never persist outside your environment.
[02:36] Dr. Laura: Can you put that in writing and is that part of the DPA/BAA?
[02:41] Priya: Yes, we'll include the no-training-on-customer-data clause in the DPA. For PHI we typically recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with a BAA — we'll get legal involved.
[02:53] [03:02] Speaker 1 (inaudible): ...uh-huh, yeah we had a question on PII detection — do you provide redaction or automatic PII scrubbing?
[03:12] Daniel: We have optional PII detection tooling and pattern-based redaction that can run pre-ingest as a webhook or via client-side libraries; we don't want to change customer content unless configured. For PHI workloads we recommend client-side redaction plus Private deployment.
[03:35] Michael: For compliance we're going to need the SOC2, ISO, pen test, and the DPA/BAA. Also want to know about data residency — does Redwood store data in specific regions?
[03:45] Daniel: In hosted, data resides in the cloud region you select (us-west-2, eu-west-1, etc). For enterprise customers we can restrict to region and provide contractual residency guarantees. Dedicated/Private of course stays in your VPC or on-prem.
[03:58] James: About 'no training' — is that a technical enforcement or contractual? Could we get logs or proof that none of our prompts were used for model updates?
[04:10] Sofia: It's both. Contractually we guarantee no training on customer-provided data unless you opt in. Technically, our training pipeline is separate and access-controlled — we can provide attestation and sampling logs. For ultra-sensitive cases, Private deployment avoids the question entirely.
[04:29] Dr. Laura: What about redaction guarantees? If an engineer accidentally includes PHI, can Redwood automatically purge or flag?
[04:36] Daniel: We provide tooling to flag and purge content via API. There's also an immediate deletion API and admin console controls — but purging across caches (KV cache, streaming buffers) has caveats; we document the purge flow. For example, KV cache lives per session and we can flush keys, but edge caches might take short time to fully expire. We'll share the doc.
[05:05] Michael: Can you walk through the audit trail example — who can see prompts, who can download logs, how is RBAC enforced?
[05:12] Daniel: RBAC enforces roles like Owner, Admin, Developer, Auditor. Audit logs capture API calls, user actions, role changes. Admins can export logs, Auditors can be given read-only log access. SSO + SCIM enforces provisioning.
[05:35] [08:02] James: We run a lot of dev/test usage; can we configure tenant-level bypass or filtering so that test traffic doesn't show up in production logs?
[08:12] Daniel: Yes — we support route-level tagging and environment segregation, plus we can set separate projects with independent retention.
[09:00] Michael: Are there any known gaps or limitations we should be aware of?
[09:06] Daniel: Two practical notes: 1) Hosted default retention is 30 days — ask for contract if you need 0 or on-request deletion; 2) Purge semantics for streaming or cached tokens require coordination for fully immutable backups — we document the guarantee and the technical caveats.
[09:34] Dr. Laura: Regarding BAA — do you sign BAAs for hosted customers or require Private?
[09:41] Sofia: We do sign BAAs; for full PHI compliance many customers prefer Dedicated or Private but we will work with you and legal to put proper controls in place.
[10:02] Michael: On the encryption front, can we rotate keys and have a key rotation schedule that Redwood honors?
[10:10] Daniel: With CMEK you control rotation. For hosted where keys are Redwood-managed we rotate keys per our policy and provide notice; with dedicated we can do BYOK.
[10:25] [20:00] Laura: A quick question on logging of personally identifying attributes — do you store raw PII in transcripts?
[20:08] Daniel: If the transcript contains PII, it's stored as provided unless you enable pre-ingest PII scrubbing. We recommend pattern-based redaction and client-side scrubbing for PHI. If you want, we can run a small eval to demonstrate redaction hooks.
[20:30] James: Can we get a technical runbook for incident response and forensic access? Our security team will need SLAs around breach notification and access to logs.
[20:38] Priya: We'll attach our incident response summary and procedure; breach notification timelines are in contract and we can confirm specific SLA windows.
[20:52] [32:00] Michael: A compliance question — do you have third-party certs for pen test and vulnerability scanning?
[32:06] Sofia: We run regular pen tests with third-party vendors and will share redacted reports. We also have automated scanning in CI/CD and publish a summary of vulnerabilities and our mitigation cadence.
[32:35] Dr. Laura: One more on data residency: if we need EU-only storage and processing, is there additional cost or delay?
[32:42] Daniel: You can select eu-west-1 and we provision in that region; depending on capacity and dedicated hardware requests there may be lead times but it's supported.
[33:00] [40:00] James: For the PoC, we want a network diagram showing VPC peering and egress rules. Can the SE provide that?
[40:07] Daniel: Yes — I'll produce a PoC network diagram and include config examples for VPC peering, security groups, and egress rules.
[40:20] Michael: Final confirmation — Redwood will not use our prompts to train public models. We need a signed statement and inclusion in the DPA.
[40:30] Sofia: We'll provide a signed attestation and include the clause in the DPA.
[40:40] Dr. Laura: And the BAA?
[40:43] Priya: We'll route the BAA draft to legal, and Sofia will introduce legal contacts.
[41:00] [49:30] Sofia: Quick recap: 1) Redwood to share SOC2/ISO/pen test artifacts; 2) Redwood legal to circulate DPA + no-training attestation + BAA draft; 3) SE to provide PoC network diagram and retention docs; 4) Schedule PoC kickoff week of 2026-03-09.
[49:50] Michael: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? We'll confirm internal stakeholders and timelines.
[49:58] James: We'll also prepare sample prompt sets (redacted) to test in the PoC, focusing on PHI scenarios.
[50:05] Sofia: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the artifact pack.
[50:12] [52:00] Meeting end.
